map.多半是 schema 版本不一致：Protobuf 靠字段编号（而非名称）识别字: Most likely a schema version mismatch: Protobuf identifies fields by number rather than name, so if the sender and receiver use different versions of the .proto, the same number is interpreted with a completely different meaning — and no error is raised. Make sure the .proto you parse with matches the sender exactly, and maintain backward compatibility by never reusing a retired field number.

map.先对 .proto 源码做词法切分得到记号序列，再用递归下降解析：顶层依次识别: The .proto source is first lexically tokenized, then parsed by recursive descent: the top level recognizes syntax, package, import, option, message, enum, and service declarations in turn. Field parsing first reads consecutive repeated / optional / required modifiers, then the type name (continuing to append on dots into a fully qualified type name), then the field name; on an equals sign the following token is parsed as an integer field number; on a bracket it reads "key = value" pairs item by item into field options, comma-separated, ending with a semicolon. oneof parsing reads the name and several "type name = number" fields inside braces. message parsing dispatches tokens inside braces: message recurses, enum parses an enum, oneof parses a union, reserved reads the comma-separated number list up to the semicolon, option reads a key-value pair, and everything else is treated as a normal field. When reading, if the current token does not match the expected one, it throws an "expected token" parse error
